parts.name: Agent plugins
parts.caption: Which hooks each agent runs
parts.description: Small config folders for Claude Code and agy. They decide which of the agent's events reach the studio.

parts.name: Hook
parts.caption: Records every agent event
parts.description: Runs on each agent event and appends it to the event log. It also holds a question or a blocked command until you answer.

parts.name: Core
parts.caption: Turns events into session state
parts.description: Plain Rust logic. It reads the event log's lines in order and knows every session's turns, checks, subagents and whether it needs you.

parts.name: Shell
parts.caption: Reads the log, feeds the core, acts
parts.description: The app's Rust side. It reads the event log, feeds the core, and carries out what follows: notices, sounds, GitHub, the terminals, the map and the CI result it reads from the default branch for the Map view, and the quiet log of what you use of it.

parts.name: Understanding
parts.caption: Writes what you read, and keeps it
parts.description: Decides what a change is worth telling you, asks the writer for it, and stores it: cards, turn summaries, briefs, the offers record and the risk notes of blocked commands.

parts.name: Window
parts.caption: Everything you see and press
parts.description: The list, the rail, Home, the Map view and the terminal panes. It shows state and sends your actions to the shell.

parts.name: Terminal daemon
parts.caption: Owns the terminals
parts.description: A background process that keeps every terminal alive, so they outlive the app.

parts.name: Workbench
parts.caption: Worktrees, PRs and plan usage
parts.description: Git worktrees, tasks, PR lookups and plan usage. A black box: it never fogs and never asks for your time.

laws.text: The hook never makes the agent wait, except for your answer.
The core does no I/O except reading transcripts.
A check's result is its last run's.
Nothing on the main thread takes the notices' lock.
The window's types and the Rust wire types agree.
A session's pieces are written one at a time, in order.
A stored file of an older format still loads.
A change is untrusted text: the writer has no tools.
Delete never ends a terminal another live session uses.
Colour is only for what needs you.

hops.text: Core sees the turn end and the shell asks for a card.
The shell passes the request on; understanding queues it for the session.
Understanding asks the writer for the card.
The writer's card comes back and understanding stores it.
Understanding tells the shell the card is stored.
The shell updates the list and sends the notice.
